title: A Prospective, Randomized, Placebo-Controlled Double Blind, 18 Month Study Evaluating the Efficacy and Tolerability of Lithium Orotate 10 mg Daily in Patients With Alzheimer's Disease and Mild Cognitive Impairment.
official: Efficacy and Tolerability of Lithium Orotate in Alzheimer's Disease and Mild Cognitive Impairment
summary:
This is a prospective, multi-center, randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind clinical trial lasting 18 months. Participants will be randomized to 1:1 to Lithium Orotate or matching placebo. Double-blinding will be maintained for investigators, participants, and outcome assessors. An independent data monitoring committee will oversee safety. The study will utilize Lithium Orotate 5 mg twice daily. The U.S. Manufacturer is Nitricost. It is a synthetic, stable Lithium Salt. The Nutricost 5 mg capsules only contain Lithium Orotate. There is no Lithium Carbonate in the 5 mg product. The Lithium Carbonate is undesirable because it is sequestered in Amyloid Plaques. The Lithium Orotate has been shown to be resist degradation and sequestration by the Amyloid Plaques.

Recruitment is 6 months.

Treatment phase is 18 months. Follow up is 1 month for post treatment for safety.

Inclusion Criteria is adults aged 50-90 years; Diagnosis of probable Alzheimer's Disease (per NIA-AA criteria) or MCI (per Peterson criteria). Baseline MMSE score of 18-26 (for AD) or 24-30 (for MCI). Participants must be stable on approved AD medications (if applicable) for \>3 months. Participants must provide informed consent (or via legally authorized representative).

Exclusion Criteria includes: Severe renal impairment of eGFR \<40, or CKD III-IV, History of Bipolar disorder or other lithium contraindications, Concomitant use of medications interacting with Lithium (e.g., diuretics, NSAIDs), Significant comorbidities (e.g., uncontrolled hypertension, recent stroke), Pregnancy or breastfeeding,

The Risk Benefit Ratio is extremely low. 1/100. The relative risk of using Lithium Orotate is extremely small compared to the possible significant benefits. The FDA has cleared the use of Lithium Orotate in this clinical trial.

The Sample Size is 200 participants (100 per arm), powered to detect a 2-point difference in MMSE change (SD=4, a+-=0.05, power=80%, 20% attrition). Stratification by AD/MCI status and age.

The Active Arm is Lithium Orotate capsules 10 mg orally daily. The Placebo Arm is Identical placebo capsules daily. Dosing of Lithium Orotate will be titrated down to 5 mg QD, if needed for tolerability. Compliance will be assessed via pill counts and patient diaries.

The Primary Endpoint is change in MMSE score from baseline, assessed every 3 months. Secondary Endpoint is PET Scan changes of Amyloid burden and/or Tau pathology at baseline and 18 months. PET Scans are optional only for participants that have an allergy to the PET Scan radionuclide, or have significant difficulty in transfers or transports to the imaging facility. Some participants will likely be home bound and unable to comply.

Safety and Incidence of adverse events (AEs), serious AEs and discontinuations will be monitored via common terminology criteria for adverse events (CTCAE).

Tolerability will be monitored via vital signs, renal functions (eGFR), thyroid function (TSH) and electrolyte panels every 3 months.
